title: Label/RichTextLabel: changing text while visible_characters = len(text) gets into an inconsistent and buggy state
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.0.stable, 4.6.3.stable, 4.7.beta3

(did not test before 4.0)

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta3 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I've discovered a little bundle of bugs relating to this specific behaviour on both `Label` and `RichTextLabel`:

1. Setting `visible_characters` to the exact length of the string (or in the case of `RichTextLabel`, to the `get_total_character_count`), then
2. Changing `text` to a longer string.

Firstly, this has inconsistent behaviour compared to if `visible_characters` is less than the length of the string:

- If `visible_characters` is -1, `visible_ratio` is always 1.0 and nothing unusual happens.
- If `visible_characters` is between 0 (inclusive) and length (exclusive), then the `visible_ratio` is used as the "source of truth" and the new string is truncated to the same percentage. For example, if len=10 and `visible_characters` is 5, changing to a len=26 string will cause 13 characters to be displayed. This appears to be the intended behaviour, though it is not documented.
- If `visible_characters` is equal to (or longer) than the text length, then `visible_characters` is used as the "source of truth" and the new string is truncated to the same number of characters as before. For example, if len=10 and `visible_characters` is 10, changing to a len=26 string will cause 10 characters to be displayed. This is weirdly inconsistent with the less-than behaviour, and also inconsistent with the -1 behaviour in which `visible_ratio` is 1.0.

Secondly, once this condition is hit, it is in an inconsistent state and multiple bugs manifest:

1. `visible_ratio` is still 1.0, even though not all of the characters are visible. (In the above example, you have text length of 26, `visible_characters` is 10, and 10 characters are displayed, however `visible_ratio` is 1.0.)
2. Attempting to set `visible_ratio` to 1.0 has no effect. This is a consequence of the above: because `visible_ratio` is already 1.0, its setter early-exits because the value is not changing. This is the **real** problem here: if you are trying to have a clean slate and both write to `text` and set `visible_ratio = 1.0`, your text will actually be truncated.

(The workaround here is to never write `visible_ratio = 1.0`, always instead write `visible_characters = -1`, but it is not obvious that you should do this. They should be equivalent.)

Related bug (but I don't think this covers the entire issue): #83387

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a `Label` (or `RichTextLabel`) with `text = "Short text"` (len=10).
2. Set `visible_characters = 10`, the exact length of the text. (This sets `visible_ratio` to 1.0.)
3. Set `text` to a new, longer string, `"Very long text, so so long"` (len=26). (This erroneously causes the text to appear truncated as "Very long ", even though `visible_ratio` remains at 1.0. It **should** reveal the entire text.)
4. Set `visible_ratio = 1.0`. This has no effect, and the text remains truncated.

Note the very different circumstance if you set `visible_characters = 9`. This sets `visible_ratio` to 0.9, and switching over to the longer text keeps `visible_ratio` at 0.9, changing `visible_characters` to 23, correctly keeping the same ratio.

You can replicate this using the UI in my MRP below (or just play with the values in the editor).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[visible_ratio_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28334714/visible_ratio_test.zip)
